llm.summary: The skill is coherent for using Anthropic through OOMOL, but its first-time setup tells users to execute unverified remote installer scripts directly.

dimensions.detail: Routine action execution is limited to Bash(oo *) and OOMOL-connected Anthropic actions, but the documented installer path would execute arbitrary remote code if followed outside that limited tool surface.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First-time setup includes direct curl-to-bash and Invoke-RestMethod-to-Invoke-Expression installer commands from cli.oomol.com without version pinning, checksum, signature, or local review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger description is broad for any Anthropic request, but the runtime instructions narrow actual operation to listed oo connector schema and run commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not install background services, modify agent memory, or request privilege escalation itself; any persistence risk comes from the external installer whose behavior is not pinned or verifiable in the skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, allowed oo CLI connector use, Anthropic actions, and server-side credential handling fit an Anthropic integration skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the installer path before installing. Prefer installing the oo CLI from a pinned, signed, or checksum-verified release channel, and do not run the provided remote script commands from an elevated shell. Once oo is already installed and connected, the skill's Anthropic connector usage is disclosed and reasonably scoped.
llm.findings:
[SC2] unexpected: Verified in artifact/SKILL.md: the install instructions pipe remote shell and PowerShell scripts directly into interpreters. Installing the oo CLI is purpose-related, but this execution pattern is broader and less verifiable than necessary.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad activation wording is present, but the body constrains actions to Anthropic connector operations through oo and does not by itself create hidden or unrelated behavior.
[SDI-4] expected: The write label on create_message is conservative but somewhat imprecise; it prompts confirmation before sending an inference request rather than hiding a durable data mutation.
[T03] unexpected: The SARIF remote payload findings are supported by the artifact lines containing curl | bash and irm | iex installer commands; this is the material Review concern.
